key_facts.fact: Expo SDK 57 is the current stable release; expo@57.0.24 is npm `latest` (published 2026-09-18). SDK 58 is in beta since Sept 15, 2026 (expo@next = 58.0.0-preview.6) with React Native 0.88 RC.
SDK 57 was released June 30, 2026 and updates React Native to 0.86.x (bundledNativeModules pins react-native 0.86.3, react 19.2.3). Upgrade command: npx expo install expo@^57.0.0 --fix.
docs.expo.dev/versions/latest lists SDK 57.0.0 with React Native 0.86, React 19.2.3, minimum Node 22.13.x.
"SDK 55 and later run entirely on the New Architecture. The New Architecture is always enabled and cannot be disabled." (legacy only on SDK 54 or earlier).

`npx create-expo-app@latest` uses the `default` template, which "Includes recommended tools such as Expo CLI, Expo Router library and TypeScript configuration enabled." Other templates: blank, blank-typescript (no router), tabs (Router + TS), bare-minimum. Flags: --template, --example, --yes, --no-install, --no-agents-md.

SDK 57 default template (expo-template-default 57.0.26) uses src/app with NativeTabs from 'expo-router/unstable-native-tabs', app.json web.output 'static', experiments.typedRoutes true and reactCompiler true, TypeScript ~6.0.3, react-native-web ~0.21.0.

SDK 58 beta: try with `npx create-expo-app@latest --template default@next` or `npx expo install expo@next --fix`; breaking changes include expo-file-system File.write() becoming async (use writeSync), expo-sqlite libSQL removal, expo-localization iOS RTL now following I18nManager; native tabs, middleware, data loaders and SSR are stable.

expo-camera supports Android, iOS, Web, Expo Go; API is CameraView + useCameraPermissions + takePictureAsync({quality, base64, exif, skipProcessing}); on web "Image URIs are always returned as base64 strings"; config plugin keys cameraPermission and microphonePermission.

expo-image-picker supports Android, iOS, Web, Expo Go; mediaTypes is now an array (['images']); on web launchers must be called inside user activation, cancel is not reported, permission requests "do nothing on web", and the asset includes a web-only `file: File`.

expo-image-manipulator supports Android, iOS, tvOS, Web, Expo Go; use ImageManipulator.manipulate(uri).resize().renderAsync() then saveAsync({compress, format: SaveFormat.JPEG, base64}); manipulateAsync is deprecated.

expo-speech supports Android, iOS, Web, Expo Go; Speech.speak(text, {language (BCP 47), voice (identifier), pitch, rate, volume, onDone...}); getAvailableVoicesAsync returns Voice{identifier,name,language,quality}; pause/resume are iOS+web only; iOS silent mode mutes it; onError not on web.

expo-print: printToFileAsync({html,width,height,base64,margins}) returns {uri, numberOfPages, base64?}; "On Web this method opens the print dialog" (no PDF file); printAsync "On web this prints the HTML from the page."

expo-sharing on web relies on the Web Share API with "very limited browser support", requires HTTPS, and "Sharing local files by URI works on Android and iOS, but not on web." Gate with Sharing.isAvailableAsync().

expo-secure-store platforms are Android, iOS, tvOS, Expo Go — web is not supported; "some iOS releases refused values above roughly 2048 bytes"; requireAuthentication unsupported in Expo Go; iOS keychain data persists across reinstall.

expo-sqlite supports Android, iOS, macOS, tvOS, Web ("Web support is in alpha and may be unstable"), Expo Go; web needs metro assetExts 'wasm' plus Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: credentialless and Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin headers; expo-sqlite/kv-store is an AsyncStorage drop-in.

@react-native-async-storage/async-storage is installed via `npx expo install @react-native-async-storage/async-storage` and supports Android, iOS, macOS, tvOS, Web, Expo Go; Expo SDK 57 pins version 2.2.0 while npm latest is 3.1.1.

expo-file-system (new File/Directory/Paths API) lists platforms Android, iOS, tvOS, Expo Go — no web; legacy API available at 'expo-file-system/legacy'; File.downloadFileAsync(url, directory) downloads files.
expo-localization supports Android, iOS, tvOS, Web, Expo Go; getLocales()[0] gives languageTag, languageCode, regionCode, textDirection; currencyCode and measurementSystem are null on web.

"RTL support is enabled by default. Layout direction follows React Native's I18nManager." Config plugin options supportsRTL (false to opt out), forcesRTL (true to force), supportedLocales; on web set `<View dir={getLocales()[0].textDirection || 'ltr'}>`; textDirection unavailable on Firefox/older browsers; runtime I18nManager.forceRTL + Updates.reloadAsync is native-only.
I18nManager.allowRTL()/forceRTL() changes "take effect on the next application start, not immediately" and persist; forceRTL is meant for development/testing.

expo-haptics supports Android, iOS, Web (browser vibration API; may be ignored in some contexts); impactAsync/notificationAsync/selectionAsync/performAndroidHapticsAsync; VIBRATE permission auto-added.

expo-image supports Android, iOS, tvOS, Web, Expo Go with contentFit, placeholder (blurhash/thumbhash), transition, cachePolicy, recyclingKey, alt; web uses with responsivePolicy/srcset and loading prop.

expo-document-picker getDocumentAsync({type:'application/pdf', multiple, copyToCacheDirectory, base64(web)}) returns {canceled, assets[{uri,name,size,mimeType, file(web)}]}; web requires user activation and cancel events are unreliable.

expo-clipboard on web uses the AsyncClipboard API which "might behave differently between browsers or not be fully supported"; getStringAsync prompts for clipboard-read permission; a WebKit issue "makes this API unusable in asynchronous code".

expo-speech-recognition (jamsch, community) latest 57.1.0 with SDK-aligned dist-tags; requires a development build (not Expo Go); iOS 17+, Android 12+; web via Web Speech API on Chrome, Safari 16+, Edge (not Firefox/Brave); config plugin microphonePermission/speechRecognitionPermission/androidSpeechServicePackages.

expo-router@57.0.22 is current (SDK-aligned versioning); route notation: _layout.tsx, index.tsx, [param].tsx, (group), +not-found.tsx, +html.tsx, +native-intent.tsx, +middleware.ts; src/app takes precedence over app/.

Native tabs import path is 'expo-router/unstable-native-tabs' on SDK 54–57 and stable 'expo-router/native-tabs' on SDK 58+; on web native tabs fall back to a basic implementation and docs recommend _layout.web.tsx with expo-router/ui.
Typed routes are enabled via experiments.typedRoutes: true in app.json; Expo CLI generates a git-ignored expo-env.d.ts; Link href and router.push become type-checked.
web.output is one of single (SPA, "Defaults to `single`"), static (HTML per route), server (static HTML + API routes); export with `npx expo export --platform web` to dist/.

Static export: set web.output 'static', run `npx expo export --platform web`, output is dist/ (public/ copied in), test with `npx serve dist`; deployable to Netlify, Vercel, Cloudflare Pages, GitHub Pages, etc.

Hosting recipes: EAS Hosting via `eas deploy`; Vercel via vercel.json {buildCommand: 'expo export -p web', outputDirectory: 'dist', rewrites to '/'}; Netlify via public/_redirects `/* /index.html 200` and `netlify deploy --dir dist`; GitHub Pages via experiments.baseUrl + gh-pages.

EAS Hosting: `npx expo export --platform web` then `eas deploy` (first run picks a subdomain, URLs like https://my-app.expo.app); runs on Cloudflare Workers with partial Node.js support; API routes supported with server output; custom domains are paid-plan only.

EAS Free plan: $0, "15 Android and 15 iOS builds" per month on a low-priority queue, 45-minute build timeout, 1 concurrency, no large workers; EAS Update 1K MAU; EAS Submit included; EAS Hosting 100,000 requests, 1,000,000 CPU-ms, 1 GB storage, 5 aliases. Starter $19/mo, Production $199/mo; usage builds $1 Android / $2 iOS medium.

EAS Build compiles iOS on "macOS runners hosted in Expo's macOS cloud" (no local Mac needed); setup: npm install --global eas-cli, eas login, eas build:configure, eas build --platform ios|android|all; Apple Developer Program $99/yr and Google Play $25 one-time are required for store distribution.

EAS Submit: `eas submit --platform ios` (needs paid Apple Developer account, ascAppId, Apple ID or ASC API key; "you don't need a Mac to ship iOS builds") and `eas submit --platform android` (.aab, Google service account JSON, first release to internal track); `eas build --auto-submit` chains them.

eas.json: cli.appVersionSource 'remote' (recommended since EAS CLI 12) with build.production.autoIncrement true lets EAS manage ios.buildNumber / android.versionCode; app.json `version` is the user-facing store version.

Store identifiers: ios.bundleIdentifier ("needs to be unique on the App Store") and android.package (reverse-DNS, "unique on the Play Store"); ios.infoPlist adds Info.plist keys such as NSCameraUsageDescription; ios.privacyManifests writes PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy; android.permissions / android.blockedPermissions control the manifest.
Permission strings go in ios.infoPlist (or library config plugins); "Changes to the Info.plist cannot be updated over-the-air, they will only be deployed when you submit a new native binary".

Apple privacy manifests: "Apple does not correctly parse all the PrivacyInfo files included by static CocoaPods dependencies (such as Expo SDK packages…)", so declare required-reason APIs in app.json ios.privacyManifests.NSPrivacyAccessedAPITypes (e.g. NSPrivacyAccessedAPICategoryUserDefaults, reason CA92.1).

Expo Go "cannot use third-party libraries that require custom native code" and "is limited and not useful for building production-grade projects"; development builds (expo-dev-client; `eas build --profile development` or `npx expo run:ios|android`) are strongly recommended.

As of May 2026 the App Store version of Expo Go supports SDK 54 while newer SDK versions await Apple approval; `eas go` builds your own Expo Go to TestFlight (requires Apple Developer membership); SDK 57/58 Expo Go is otherwise only available via Expo CLI for Android devices and iOS simulators.

React Native accessibility props: accessible, accessibilityLabel, accessibilityHint, accessibilityRole, accessibilityState, accessibilityValue, accessibilityLiveRegion, importantForAccessibility, accessibilityActions/onAccessibilityAction, plus aria-* aliases and a `role` prop that takes priority over accessibilityRole.

AccessibilityInfo exposes isScreenReaderEnabled, isReduceMotionEnabled, isBoldTextEnabled (iOS), isHighTextContrastEnabled (Android), isDarkerSystemColorsEnabled (iOS), isInvertColorsEnabled, isGrayscaleEnabled, isReduceTransparencyEnabled, announceForAccessibility, announceForAccessibilityWithOptions, sendAccessibilityEvent (setAccessibilityFocus deprecated).

Text: allowFontScaling defaults to true ("respect Text Size accessibility settings"); maxFontSizeMultiplier caps scaling (0 = no max, >=1 = cap); iOS dynamicTypeRamp (caption2…largeTitle, default body); adjustsFontSizeToFit + minimumFontScale.
PixelRatio.getFontScale() returns the font-size scaling factor from Android Settings > Display > Font size or iOS Text Size / Larger Text.

React Native docs state no minimum touch-target size; Pressable offers hitSlop ("additional distance outside of element in which a press can be detected") and pressRetentionOffset. The 44pt/48dp minimums are Apple HIG / Material guidance, not RN docs.

Dark mode: app.json userInterfaceStyle 'automatic' | 'light' | 'dark'; use useColorScheme() or Appearance.getColorScheme()/addChangeListener from react-native; Android development builds need expo-system-ui installed or userInterfaceStyle is ignored.

Unit testing: `npx expo install jest-expo jest @types/jest --dev`, package.json "jest": {"preset": "jest-expo"}, script "test": "jest --watchAll", add "jest" to tsconfig types; `npx expo install @testing-library/react-native --dev`; RNTL replaces deprecated react-test-renderer (no React 19 support).

jest-expo presets: jest-expo (default), jest-expo/ios, jest-expo/android, jest-expo/web, jest-expo/node, jest-expo/universal; platform tests via -test.ios.tsx etc.; snapshots saved per platform (.snap.ios, .snap.web).
@testing-library/react-native 14.0.1 peer deps: jest >=29 (optional), react >=19, react-native >=0.78, test-renderer ^1.0.0; matchers are built in once you import from the library.

Type checking: docs say run `tsc` from the project root; expo/tsconfig.base sets noEmit: true (plus jsx react-jsx, moduleResolution bundler, customConditions ['react-native'], skipLibCheck), so `npx tsc` and `npx tsc --noEmit` behave the same; generate tsconfig with `npx expo customize tsconfig.json`; enable strict; path alias @/* -> src/*.

warnings: Do not install `react-native@latest` (0.87.1) or `@react-native-async-storage/async-storage@latest` (3.1.1) by hand: Expo SDK 57 pins react-native 0.86.3 and async-storage 2.2.0. Always add packages with `npx expo install <pkg>` and fix drift with `npx expo install --fix`.

`--template blank-typescript` does NOT include Expo Router (entry is index.ts). Use the `default` template (Router + TS + native tabs + typed routes) or `tabs` (Router + TS, lighter) for a file-based-routing app.

The SDK 57 default template imports `NativeTabs` from `expo-router/unstable-native-tabs`; that path becomes `expo-router/native-tabs` in SDK 58. Native tabs only fall back to a basic layout on web — add a `_layout.web.tsx` with `expo-router/ui` (or use JS `Tabs` everywhere) if web parity matters.

SDK 58 (beta now, stable within weeks) changes `File.write()` to async (use `File.writeSync()` for the old behavior), removes expo-sqlite libSQL, makes `web.output: server` the default when API routes are used, and changes iOS RTL to follow I18nManager. If you start on 57 today, plan a 58 upgrade before store submission (iOS 27 scene-based lifecycle support lands there).

Web is NOT supported by expo-secure-store or the new expo-file-system API (neither lists web). Branch on `Platform.OS === 'web'`: keep secrets out of storage or use an explicitly unencrypted fallback, and handle files via the `file`/`base64` fields that expo-image-picker / expo-document-picker return on web.

PDF export on web does not produce a file: `Print.printToFileAsync` "opens the print dialog" on web, and `Sharing.shareAsync` cannot share local URIs on web and needs HTTPS + Web Share API support. Use a browser-side approach (e.g. print-to-PDF via the dialog, or a JS PDF library / server render) for web.

expo-sqlite on web is alpha and requires COEP `credentialless` + COOP `same-origin` headers and a `wasm` Metro asset extension; static hosts (Vercel/Netlify) need explicit header config, and these headers can break third-party embeds. Consider AsyncStorage or IndexedDB for the web tier if you cannot control headers.

On web, expo-image-picker, expo-document-picker and expo-clipboard reads must run synchronously inside the user gesture handler (no awaits before the call); cancel events are not reported by browsers, so never block UI waiting for `canceled`.

expo-speech-recognition (community, jamsch) requires a development build — it will not load in Expo Go — and only works on Chrome/Safari 16+/Edge on web (not Firefox/Brave); iOS 17+/Android 12+ only. Add NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription via its config plugin.

expo-speech on iOS is silent when the ringer switch is on silent; Android lacks pause/resume; voice availability (especially for non-English/RTL languages) varies by device/browser — query `getAvailableVoicesAsync()` and fall back to `language` only.

Expo Go on the App Store was still at SDK 54 as of May 2026; SDK 57/58 Expo Go is only available via Expo CLI (Android/iOS simulator) or `eas go` (TestFlight, needs Apple Developer account). Build a development build (`eas build --profile development`) from day one — it is also required for config-plugin permission strings and any custom native module.

EAS Free plan limits: 15 iOS + 15 Android builds per month, low-priority queue, 45-minute timeout, 1 concurrent build, no large workers. Budget builds (use `--profile preview` internal builds sparingly) or expect to move to Starter ($19/mo).

Store submission prerequisites are external: Apple Developer Program ($99/yr, app record created in App Store Connect for `ascAppId`) and Google Play Developer ($25 one-time, service-account JSON, first Android release lands on the internal track and store listing must be completed manually). EAS Submit uploads binaries only — no metadata/screenshots.

Permission strings and privacy manifests are baked into the binary: changing `ios.infoPlist`, config-plugin permission text, or `ios.privacyManifests` requires a new EAS build and store submission (not OTA). Expo's guide says Apple may not read PrivacyInfo from static-pod dependencies, so declare required-reason APIs (e.g. UserDefaults CA92.1) yourself.

Runtime RTL switching (`I18nManager.forceRTL`) only applies after an app restart and does nothing on web; on web set the `dir` attribute from `getLocales()[0].textDirection` (null on Firefox). Test both directions with the `forcesRTL` plugin option in separate dev builds.

React Native docs give no minimum touch-target size; the 44×44 pt / 48×48 dp figures are Apple HIG / Material guidance (not verified from RN docs). Enforce with `minHeight/minWidth: 44` and `hitSlop`.

`allowFontScaling` is on by default — layouts must survive 2×+ font scale; cap only where truncation would break meaning using `maxFontSizeMultiplier`. There is no Expo high-contrast helper; combine `useColorScheme()` with `AccessibilityInfo.isHighTextContrastEnabled()` (Android) / `isDarkerSystemColorsEnabled()` (iOS).

@testing-library/react-native 14 needs the new `test-renderer` package (peer `^1.0.0`); the Expo unit-testing guide's install command does not include it, so add `npm i -D test-renderer` if render() fails. Remove any `react-test-renderer` (deprecated, no React 19 support).

Typed routes generate `expo-env.d.ts` only after `npx expo start` (or `npx expo customize tsconfig.json`) runs; CI type-check (`npx tsc --noEmit`) will fail on typed `href`s until that file exists — run `npx expo customize tsconfig.json` or start the CLI once in CI before `tsc`.
